newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs back off on Nikkei gains.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs back off on Nikkei gains.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures came under pressure in relatively light trade on Friday as players liquidated their positions following a late rebound in Tokyo stocks.

Sentiment was also cautious ahead of the release of U.S. non-farm payrolls data, due at 1330 GMT. Economists in a Reuters poll estimated on average that payrolls rose by 230,000 jobs in February after growing by 271,000 in January.
"Everyone is jittery. Maybe they want to square some longs ahead of the weekend," said a dealer at a Japanese institution.
December Euroyen was quoted at 99.19 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.21 on volume of 6,100 lots. June JGBs settled at 125.21 against their previous 125.34.

Dealers said Nomura Securities Co Ltd's disclosure that its directors had been involved in apparently irregular deals had little impact on the market, but the news could be a factor next week if more details emerged.
Eurodollar futures came off on fairly active volumes as players braced themselves for the U.S. employment figures.

"There is still the lingering idea that the U.S. may raise rates so everyone is looking to sell some first," said the trader, adding that a higher-than-expected rise in payrolls would reinforce fears of an interest rate hike.
"The reaction everyone is expecting is a bit of a sell-off tonight so we'd need an extremely friendly number for it not to go down," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.
June Eurodollars ended at 94.145 against their IMM close at 94.160 on turnover of 16,095 lots. September were at 93.930 against 93.945 on 13,665 lots.
